doc.title: Cedar Walton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Audiences and package shows at the Howard Theater
summary: Audiences were mixed, and at Washington's Howard Theater and Baltimore the bill had a comedian MC, singers such as Ray Charles or Betty Carter and often another jazz group.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What was your, when you, when you were in the States, um, what was the composition of the audience? I'm speaking racially.

Oh man, uh, that's a hard question, simply because of my ability to remember uh … I think it was sort of even-steven, maybe with a little edge on White in some places and uh the opposite in other places. I can't really uh verify that it was uh, uh, uh solid uh difference every, every time. It varied.
What about in Washington? Was Washington uh …
[? caramie?] spoke about the Howard Theater.
Yeah, I remember playin' there but I couldn't see exactly who was in the audience, but uh, uh I would take a guess from the make-up of your fair city that uh it was mostly Black folks.
What, what … other than Howard, were you doing … when you were in Howard, what was the bill you were on? It wasn't just Art Blakey.
No, they would have a comedian and uh probably somebody like uh either Ray Charles, Betty Carter, those kind of shows, jazz shows.
And what other … Were you doing the same thing in Baltimore or …

Yeah. Yeah. I can remember Baltimore had uh, uh Herbie uh … oh, shucks … Mann, Herbie Mann and his, you know, his group uh, uh … Hubert Laws was playin' with him then. So uh, that's some pleasant memories, but those shows in theaters uh wasn't just us. It was uh, uh a
jazz show, usually a comedian who was the MC, a good, you know, a well-known singer, and maybe another jazz group with uh a Latin tinge. And uh, that kind of thing.
